title: upfly optimize --json: the result
description: The last line upfly optimize --json prints when the run finishes: the plan, what an applied run wrote, and the report. Without --apply nothing is written and run is null. Progress and diagnostic lines come before it (events.json); a run that stops or refuses prints an error line instead (events.json).

apply.description: Whether --apply was given, so the plan was written.

planHash.description: SHA-256 of the plan's conversions and rewrites, and its removals when it has any, as plan gives them: a dry run's, which optimize --apply --expect-plan takes back to write only that plan, or an applied run's before its first write.

only.description: With --only or --image: the images they named, and each pattern, or path given with --image, that named none. null without either.

applyRefusals.description: On a dry run, each note that says what --apply would refuse, with the reason its error line would give, such as UNCOMMITTED_CHANGES or NO_REPOSITORY. Each note is also in notes. Empty with --apply.

plan.description: What the run converts and rewrites, or with --remove-originals what it removes, and what it decided against. The same with and without --apply.

rewrites.description: The references that move, one entry per file.

removals.description: With --remove-originals: each original named with --image that the run removes, its converted file standing beside it. Empty on a run that converts.

declined.description: Everything the plan decided against, each with its reason: with --remove-originals, each original named with --image that stays.

line.description: The line, counted from 1, or null when the reason is about a whole file.

keptOriginals.description: Unless originals are kept (--keep-originals, or keep-original in the config), the converted images whose original stays anyway, and why.

refusal.description: Why the plan holds nothing at all, or null. A command that meets one stops with an error line, so its result always has null.

quality.description: The quality the saving was measured at and the file is written at, or "lossless".

replacesOriginal.description: true when the original is removed: by default, unless --keep-originals or the config keeps originals, once every reference to it moves and no file Upfly reads still names it.

inPublicDir.description: true when the original sits in a folder the site is served from, such as public, where a link from outside the project (an email, another site) can name it. With replacesOriginal, such a link stops working once the run applies; the dry run counts these originals. One a build loads is published under a new name with every build, so nothing outside links to it.

removal.description: One original kept beside its converted file, which the run removes: the converted file is the same picture under the same path in the run's format, and no line in the project names the original.

converted.description: The converted file beside it, which takes its place.

inPublicDir.description: true when the original sits in a folder the site is served from, such as public, where a link from outside the project (an email, another site) can name it and stops working once it goes.

edits.description: In the order they appear in the file.

textHash.description: SHA-256 of the file's text as Upfly read it. The edits are made only to a file that still holds that text.

edit.description: One path re-spelled: a reference, or a path inside a comment. The offsets count the file's text in UTF-16 code units, as JavaScript counts a string.

expected.description: The text the edit replaces, the path as written.

inComment.description: The path is inside a comment, which no page loads. It moves with the references, and is never counted as one.

asset.description: The image the path names before the run, as a path inside the project.

run.description: What an applied run wrote, or null when it wrote nothing: a dry run, or a plan with nothing to do. Unless undoable is false, upfly undo puts every one of these files back.

id.description: The run's id, which the commit message names.

undoable.description: Given by optimize: false for a run made with --no-undo, which keeps no record once it finishes, so upfly undo leaves it as it is and still puts back the last run made without it. dedupe and move leave it out: upfly undo always puts their runs back.

commit.description: The hash of the one commit --commit made, or null.

repository.description: The git repository the project is in, or null when it is in none: top is the repository's folder, and path is the project's folder inside it, empty when they are the same.

notes.description: Things worth knowing about the run, each a sentence: on a dry run, what --apply would refuse, such as uncommitted changes; with --only, how many images it left out.
